points.description: Defines a queue as a data structure that stores elements according to the first-in, first-out (FIFO) principle. Accept equivalent wording such as 'items are removed in the same order they were added' or 'first in, first out'.
points.partial_credit: Award part marks if the answer identifies a queue as a data structure/collection but does not state the FIFO ordering, or states FIFO without describing it as a data structure.

levels.says: Says a queue is a data structure or collection for storing elements, but does not state the first-in, first-out ordering.
States the first-in, first-out principle, but does not identify a queue as a data structure or collection.

points.description: Names the main queue operations as enqueue and dequeue. Accept equivalent terms such as 'add/insert' for enqueue and 'remove/delete' for dequeue.
points.partial_credit: Award part marks if only one of the two main operations is named.

levels.says: Names only one of enqueue or dequeue (or only one equivalent add/remove operation).

rubric.notes: Full marks require a clear FIFO definition of a queue and both main operations, enqueue and dequeue. Part marks are available for a partial definition or for naming only one operation. No marks are earned for an answer that neither describes FIFO storage nor names a queue operation.
